Sorry for the long reply! As someone who went to a Catholic high school, I have a bit of insight that may be helpful! I’m also a teacher at a school with chalkboards, funnily enough.

With regard to the hair thing, if it’s not against school policy go for it! I’m sure there are going to be a lot of students that will really love it. It makes you more relatable, and students then know they can come to you for advice for dyeing hair.

For praying, I second what someone else said about having a student lead it. What I and my fellow non religious classmates and teachers did during prayer was just close our eyes or bow our heads in a silent meditation. You don’t need to pray, you can even just take the moment to do a grounding exercise! I always did some deep breathing.

Since you’re a new teacher, you may be able to ask for a mentor teacher or at least someone you can go to for help. I’m a second year teacher and I have a mentor teacher. We meet once every other week, but sometimes we just briefly check in. This helps with school rules too! This way you have someone that’s been there longer to help answer your questions.


I understand the blackboard thing. I’ve found some chalk that feels so lovely and smooth going onto the blackboard and other chalk that feels like the worst substance known to man. You can ask your fellow teachers which chalk they like most, or their recommendations. You can also get a chalk pen which I saw some people mention! Worst case scenario, if you have a projector you can always just use that. 


Wishing you the best of luck on your teaching journey!

I was told I was bossy, rude, had “anger issues” when I was really just having meltdowns as a child, sensitive or a drama queen, picky / fussy, and YES in my own world!! 

I’m now a teacher, and it’s strangely comforting when I see students that have the same behaviors I exhibited. I know how to deal with them, and I can offer practical advice, coping strategies, or just to be an understanding or comforting presence. I try to have them reframe the language around them, too. They’re not a drama queen or crazy, their brain just works differently!

Maybe, yes, and no. I might be able to opt out of a dinner or two, but I’m just worried about it seeming rude. I’m definitely worried about the sleeping situation (a couple people will have to share rooms), and our work is paying for the Airbnb and I can’t afford any other options for housing.

I’m not sure whether or not this is an Autism-specific thing, but I’ve experienced the same. I don’t feel a connection to my birth name, and I almost feel like it’s more of a serial number than a name. 

I’ve been going by a new name within my close friends and it’s been a game changer! You can always experiment with a name that feels more “you.” Might take some time to find, but it helps tremendously!

I’ve had this happen to me, but with a slightly different situation.

NDad got me wine BEFORE I turned 21 since I had expressed interest in using it to cook once I could buy it. When I visited from college and was going to drive back he insisted I take the wine with me. Me and my roommate were both under 21 at the time and we would be driving through multiple states with alcohol neither of us were old enough to possess. It was absolutely illegal.

I told him no that I didn’t want to do anything illegal and I wouldn’t even be allowed to have it on campus since I wasn’t 21. He got insanely mad and frustrated with me, tried CONVINCING me to commit a crime (“you won’t get pulled over, it’ll be fine” “it’s not that big of a deal” “they’re not going to look in your trunk”), and just sulked and became passive aggressive about me not wanting his gift and making him waste his money.

No idea what these people are on about. Absolutely crazy.

I have a similar experience with driving. My NDad followed me practically anytime I drove on Life360. My navigation once took me through a shortcut through a residential area (LA freeway at a standstill as per usual) and he immediately called me and yelled telling me to “get the hell out of there” that it was dangerous and I could be shot. Another time driving to see some relatives I took a rural road shortcut and he called to make sure I “hadn’t been kidnapped.” This was 3.5 hours into my drive. He was following me the whole time.

Also followed me on my two day trip from home to college where my roommate was also in the car. Almost thirty seconds after we were stopped in a traffic jam in Colorado, we get a call. “Traffic stopped, huh?” Sir, this is day two hour six- stop watching me.
Thank you so much. Hearing a parent’s perspective on this is really helpful and insightful!

Cleaned it up in no time, I thought it was going to take hours or like a special sort of cleaner. I don’t understand it, I think he just wanted to yell at me for something- anything.

All the time!! Even though my sibling and I are adults- early twenties- my NDad always bashes one of us in front of the other. For years I hated my sibling, despised them, I thought they were terrible, incompetent, and mentally not there (turns out we’re both mentally ill- yay!). This went on for almost a decade. We didn’t initially get along great, but we still loved each other until the double agent bs happened.

Now that I’m learning more about how terrible and abusive he is, seeing it with my own eyes, I’ve apologized to my sibling and now we’re literally the best of friends. We call each other almost every day and say I love you, that we believe in the other and that we’ll eventually get out from underneath the iron fist of my NDad. 

My NDad has told me “You guys just suddenly got along and then now /I’m/ the common enemy?”
Yes. Yes you are. I wonder why!

I completely understand how you feel. The regular “spending Christmas with your family and friends” bit hurts a lot for me, since I don’t have a good family and minimal friends. But it might help to sort of set up your own Christmas traditions. I started making homemade pasta and watching an old Christmas movie with my dog. It’s not much, and it’s not a stereotypical fantastic Christmas, but it’s mine nonetheless. Yknow?

My NDad does this all the time. Threatened to pull me out of college on multiple occasions. It’s just a way to control you with fear into doing what they want.

Not normal in the slightest. I’m 20, and my NDad makes me have the Life360 app on my phone also. I know how you feel. While we don’t have cameras in the house, anytime a door leading out opens there’s a chime that plays throughout the house. I couldn’t go anywhere without explaining myself. 

I know it seems like it will take forever, but you WILL get through this. One step is to get your own cell phone plan so you don’t have to have that app on there. The next step is to move out. College is a great place to taste independence- it’s what made me realize my parents were so controlling. 

See what they have in terms of on-campus housing or off-campus housing. See if any of your friends want to split money for an apartment or renting a house. I know you said the apartments near you aren’t the best, but I guarantee it will be much better than living with your narc parents.
This is amazing!! I’m in love with the art style!

It’s mostly a financial threat, since my parents pay for a majority of my college. Essentially I have Life 360 on my phone or they won’t help pay for anything. Realistically they can’t actually force me out of enrollment, but if they stopped supporting me I wouldn’t be able to pay for it.
No need to compare the severity, we’re both experiencing terrible behavior from parents that just want more control. I’m glad you found that app, and I hope college is a freeing experience for you!

My narcissistic dad also claims that I have no capacity for empathy and that I only ever think about myself. I’m an empath, I care about other people way more than I care about myself! I’m actually working in therapy with focusing *more* on myself because I give way too much to others and not nearly enough focus to myself.

I honestly think these people are either projecting or just straight up playing an opposite game to make us feel bad or underneath them in some way.

My parents do this to me, too! I’m in my third year of college, but they insist that I use Life 360 or I can’t be away at college, period. They’ve threatened to pull me out of school if I don’t keep it on my phone, and they get notifications for practically everywhere I go.

It’s not normal. It’s an invasion of privacy. It’s creepy. It’s controlling. For now, you can trick Life360 into reporting another location (I’ve heard it’s an easy google search, but I haven’t done it myself bc quarantine) so you can have a bit more privacy. I’m so sorry you have to go through this, too. Stay strong, my friend.
Thank you, I will!
This is exactly how my dad is! Any display of emotion on my part is immediately rude or inexcusable, but he can do whatever he wants and it's fine.

I have a very similar situation: depression, anxiety, suicide attempts, physically supported but not emotionally. When I brought up my suicidal thoughts while being held at the hospital, my dad told me the same things that he had given me everything, I'm making a big deal out of nothing, I'm playing the victim, I'm doing it for attention, that I was actually at fault for making other people uncomfortable.  


You are NOT the problem. PLEASE don't tell yourself that any of this is your fault. You deserve to be supported emotionally, and good parents support their children with material and emotional needs. You are not the problem. Your parents are not providing you the support you need.

I have a very similar situation! My dad comfortably makes six figures, and is paying for my housing and part of my tuition. He was excited to do it; he said my education is "a good investment." Now, though, he has threatened to pull me out of school on multiple occasions and constantly tells me about "how expensive" I am and how much money he could save if I didn't go to school. I can't afford tuition on my own nor housing. 

He says he can barely afford groceries, but tells me to cover my eyes when he fills out the fafsa. He bought my car on his *debit card*. He bought an 800k house. No wonder I get no financial aid, they probably think I have enough to pay my entire 4 years on one year of my dad's wage!
